AUTHORED FIGURE BRIEF:
This figure is a three-dimensional plot of a single space curve rendered in dark blue against labeled coordinate axes. The vertical z-axis is graduated with ticks and numerals at 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12. The x-axis runs toward the lower left with ticks labeled 2 and 4 in front and -2 and -4 behind, and the y-axis runs toward the lower right with the same labeling, 2 and 4 on the near side and -2 and -4 on the far side. The curve spirals counterclockwise around the vertical axis while climbing steadily, completing roughly two full turns between the xy-plane and the top of the frame above z = 12; its circular cross-section has radius 4, so each loop sweeps out past the ticks marked 4 on both horizontal axes. Two arrowheads placed on the ascending curve show the direction of travel. Across the upper right, in bold, the formula r(t) = 4cost i + 4sint j + t k is printed. Holding the loop radius constant while the height grows in step with the parameter is precisely what produces the spring-like shape. The plot displays the graph of a vector-valued function whose circular motion in the horizontal plane combines with uniform vertical rise to trace a helix.

REQUESTED INTERACTIONS:
- Animation for tracing r(t): the learner plays the motion, a point moves around the circle while rising at constant speed and leaves the helix behind, making the combination of circular horizontal motion and linear vertical motion visible.
- Slider for parameter t: the learner scrubs t, the point advances along the helix with live x=4cos(t), y=4sin(t), and z=t values, showing how the vector-valued function maps time to position.
- Toggle between top view and 3D view: the learner switches views, the helix collapses to a radius-4 circle from above and returns to a rising spiral in 3D, clarifying that constant radius and increasing height together form the helix.
- Equation input for the parametric curve: learner edits x(t), y(t), and z(t), pre-filled with 4*cos(t), 4*sin(t), and t; the helix redraws and the moving point follows the new curve over the same t interval.

SOURCE FILE: OpenStax Calculus, chapter 13: Vector-Valued Functions

PROJECTION (inspect the source image, choose exactly one, and call setCameraView accordingly):
  perspective:
    Use the scaffold's true perspective projection after building all geometry. Use this only when the source has real vanishing-point convergence or distance-based size shrinkage; then depth should visibly affect apparent size.

  axonometric:
    Use ordinary orthographic projection: setCameraView({ projection: 'orthographic', axisScreenAngles, heightFraction }). If the source is a flat 2D plot or diagram, pass axisScreenAngles: null for a front-on view. Otherwise do not try to measure per-figure angles from the image — use a standard isometric pose: axisScreenAngles: { x: 30, z: 30 }. The source image is a PROJECTION of a 3D object: rebuild the true object — a rectangle stays a rectangle in world space — and let the camera do the projecting. Never bake the drawn parallelogram into the geometry, and never shear geometry. Omit zoom and call setCameraView after all geometry is added — the scaffold auto-fits from the projected bounding box.

  oblique:
    Call setCameraView({ projection: 'oblique', obliqueAngleDeg: 45, depthScale: 0.5, heightFraction }) after all geometry is added — a standard cabinet-oblique pose; do not try to measure per-figure oblique angles from the image. The scaffold implements oblique as a shear of the eye-space projection matrix, so the front face stays undistorted, depth edges leave at obliqueAngleDeg, and labels track the shear automatically. Build the TRUE 3D object — the shear is the camera's job. Do NOT shear geometry, do NOT wrap the figure in a sheared parent Object3D, and do NOT disable automatic matrix updates. The scaffold also provides the reveal interaction: dragging eases the shear out to expose the real 3D shape and a toggle button returns to the printed view — do not implement either yourself.
AXIS ASSIGNMENT: the pose is pinned, so in BoxGeometry(w, h, d) the w axis is screen-right, h is screen-up, and d is the receding diagonal. Before writing each BoxGeometry, look at the source image and decide which of the object's dimensions actually recedes there — do not assume it is the one the domain calls "depth". In feature-map / layer-stack diagrams the channel count is usually the w (horizontal) extent along the flow direction and a spatial dimension is d. Sanity-check the silhouette against the source: a block that should read as a long bar pointing at its neighbours must be long in w, not in d, or it will render as a sliver shooting into the page. If your chosen axis assignment contradicts the source image's silhouette, follow the image.

Build the figure directly from the brief above and the source image. There is no interaction plan: decide the elements, geometry, labels, and controls yourself.

// @FIGURE_CODE_BEGIN // axes -> LineSegments(BufferGeometry) dark grey // axesArrows -> ConeGeometry(0.15, 0.4) dark grey // ghost_helix -> plotParametric3D light gray, faint // trace_helix -> plotParametric3D dark blue // tracer -> SphereGeometry(0.2) red // traceArrow -> ConeGeometry(0.25, 0.7) dark blue const T_MAX = 4 * Math.PI; // Approx 12.566 let current_t = 0; let isPlaying = false; // Coordinates mapping: // Math x -> Three Z // Math y -> Three X // Math z -> Three Y /* ── 1. Axes and Ticks ── */ const axesMat = new THREE.LineBasicMaterial({ color: 0x333333 }); const axesGeo = new THREE.BufferGeometry().setFromPoints([ new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, -6), new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 6.5), // Math x new THREE.Vector3(-6, 0, 0), new THREE.Vector3(6.5, 0, 0), // Math y new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 0), new THREE.Vector3(0, 13.5, 0) // Math z ]); scene.add(new THREE.LineSegments(axesGeo, axesMat)); const arrowGeo = new THREE.ConeGeometry(0.15, 0.4, 8); const arrowMat = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: 0x333333 }); const arrowX = new THREE.Mesh(arrowGeo, arrowMat); arrowX.position.set(0, 0, 6.5); arrowX.rotation.x = Math.PI / 2; // points to +Z scene.add(arrowX); const arrowY = new THREE.Mesh(arrowGeo, arrowMat); arrowY.position.set(6.5, 0, 0); arrowY.rotation.z = -Math.PI / 2; // points to +X scene.add(arrowY); const arrowZ = new THREE.Mesh(arrowGeo, arrowMat); arrowZ.position.set(0, 13.5, 0); scene.add(arrowZ); // Ticks const tickSize = 0.2; const tickPts = []; // Math x (Three Z) [-4, -2, 2, 4].forEach(v => { tickPts.push(new THREE.Vector3(-tickSize, 0, v), new THREE.Vector3(tickSize, 0, v)); addLabel(v.toString(), new THREE.Vector3(tickSize + 0.4, 0, v)); }); // Math y (Three X) [-4, -2, 2, 4].forEach(v => { tickPts.push(new THREE.Vector3(v, 0, -tickSize), new THREE.Vector3(v, 0, tickSize)); addLabel(v.toString(), new THREE.Vector3(v, 0, tickSize + 0.4)); }); // Math z (Three Y) [2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12].forEach(v => { tickPts.push(new THREE.Vector3(-tickSize, v, 0), new THREE.Vector3(tickSize, v, 0)); addLabel(v.toString(), new THREE.Vector3(-tickSize - 0.4, v, 0)); }); scene.add(new THREE.LineSegments(new THREE.BufferGeometry().setFromPoints(tickPts), axesMat)); // Axis labels addLabel('x', new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 7), { bold: true, fontSize: '15px' }); addLabel('y', new THREE.Vector3(7, 0, 0), { bold: true, fontSize: '15px' }); addLabel('z', new THREE.Vector3(0, 14, 0), { bold: true, fontSize: '15px' }); addLabel('r(t) = 4 cos t i + 4 sin t j + t k', new THREE.Vector3(0, 12.5, -3.5), { fontSize: '15px', color: '#111' }); /* ── 2. Parametric Plots ── */ const ghost_helix = plotParametric3D('ghost_helix', { x: '4*sin(t)', y: 't', z: '4*cos(t)', variables: ['t'], tDomain: [0, T_MAX], samples: 200, color: 0xa0a0a0 }); ghost_helix.object.material.transparent = true; ghost_helix.object.material.opacity = 0.4; const trace_helix = plotParametric3D('trace_helix', { x: '4*sin(t)', y: 't', z: '4*cos(t)', variables: ['t'], tDomain: [0, 0.001], samples: 200, color: 0x1f3b6c }); /* ── 3. Tracer Elements ── */ const tracerMat = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: 0xdc3545 }); const tracer = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.2, 16, 16), tracerMat); scene.add(tracer); registerInteractive(tracer, { title: "Vector-Valued Function", body: "The tracer marks the tip of the position vector r(t) at the current parameter value t." }); const traceArrowGeo = new THREE.ConeGeometry(0.25, 0.7, 8); traceArrowGeo.rotateX(-Math.PI / 2); // Orient so tip is at local -Z const traceArrow = new THREE.Mesh(traceArrowGeo, new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: 0x1f3b6c })); scene.add(traceArrow); /* ── 4. Interaction Logic ── */ function updatePoint() { const f_math_y = trace_helix.fx; // Three X const f_math_z = trace_helix.fy; // Three Y const f_math_x = trace_helix.fz; // Three Z let px, py, pz; try { px = f_math_x(current_t); } catch { px = NaN; } try { py = f_math_y(current_t); } catch { py = NaN; } try { pz = f_math_z(current_t); } catch { pz = NaN; } const valid = Number.isFinite(px) && Number.isFinite(py) && Number.isFinite(pz); if (valid) { tracer.position.set(py, pz, px); tracer.visible = true; let px1, py1, pz1; try { px1 = f_math_x(current_t + 1e-3); py1 = f_math_y(current_t + 1e-3); pz1 = f_math_z(current_t + 1e-3); } catch { px1 = NaN; } if (Number.isFinite(px1) && Number.isFinite(py1) && Number.isFinite(pz1)) { const dir = new THREE.Vector3(py1 - py, pz1 - pz, px1 - px); if (dir.lengthSq() > 1e-8) { traceArrow.position.set(py, pz, px); traceArrow.lookAt(py + dir.x, pz + dir.y, px + dir.z); traceArrow.visible = true; } else { traceArrow.visible = false; } } else { traceArrow.visible = false; } document.getElementById('live-x').textContent = px.toFixed(2); document.getElementById('live-y').textContent = py.toFixed(2); document.getElementById('live-z').textContent = pz.toFixed(2); } else { tracer.visible = false; traceArrow.visible = false; document.getElementById('live-x').textContent = 'NaN'; document.getElementById('live-y').textContent = 'NaN'; document.getElementById('live-z').textContent = 'NaN'; } document.getElementById('val-t').textContent = current_t.toFixed(2); trace_helix.tDomain = [0, Math.max(1e-5, current_t)]; trace_helix.sample(); } // Bind equations. Note that bindEquationInput parses the expression, and if successful, calls setX/setY/setZ. // Math x -> Three Z bindEquationInput('eq-x', [ { handle: ghost_helix, method: 'setZ' }, { handle: trace_helix, method: 'setZ' } ], { variables: ['t'], onChange: () => { if (!isPlaying) updatePoint(); } }); // Math y -> Three X bindEquationInput('eq-y', [ { handle: ghost_helix, method: 'setX' }, { handle: trace_helix, method: 'setX' } ], { variables: ['t'], onChange: () => { if (!isPlaying) updatePoint(); } }); // Math z -> Three Y bindEquationInput('eq-z', [ { handle: ghost_helix, method: 'setY' }, { handle: trace_helix, method: 'setY' } ], { variables: ['t'], onChange: () => { if (!isPlaying) updatePoint(); } }); /* ── 5. Playback and Controls ── */ const slider = document.getElementById('t-slider'); const btnPlay = document.getElementById('btn-play'); slider.addEventListener('input', (e) => { current_t = parseFloat(e.target.value); isPlaying = false; updatePlayBtn(); updatePoint(); }); function updatePlayBtn() { btnPlay.textContent = isPlaying ? 'Pause' : 'Play'; btnPlay.classList.toggle('active', isPlaying); } btnPlay.addEventListener('click', () => { isPlaying = !isPlaying; if (isPlaying && current_t >= T_MAX - 0.02) { current_t = 0; } updatePlayBtn(); }); let isTopView = false; const btnView = document.getElementById('btn-view'); btnView.addEventListener('click', () => { isTopView = !isTopView; if (isTopView) { // Camera looks down the Y axis. Math x (Three Z) points down, Math y (Three X) points right. setCameraView({ projection: 'orthographic', azimuthDeg: 0, elevationDeg: 90, heightFraction: 0.85 }); btnView.textContent = '3D View'; btnView.classList.add('active'); } else { setCameraView({ projection: 'orthographic', axisScreenAngles: { x: 30, z: 30 }, heightFraction: 0.85 }); btnView.textContent = 'Top View'; btnView.classList.remove('active'); } }); let lastTime = performance.now(); function loop() { requestAnimationFrame(loop); const now = performance.now(); const dt = (now - lastTime) / 1000; lastTime = now; if (isPlaying) { // ~5 seconds to trace the full 12.56 curve current_t += dt * (T_MAX / 5); if (current_t >= T_MAX) { current_t = T_MAX; isPlaying = false; updatePlayBtn(); } slider.value = current_t.toString(); updatePoint(); } } // Initial setup updatePoint(); setCameraView({ projection: 'orthographic', axisScreenAngles: { x: 30, z: 30 }, heightFraction: 0.85 }); loop(); // @FIGURE_CODE_END
